question: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

In a resolution adopted in June 2026, Parliament highlighted the risks associated with implementing the provisions on the quaternary treatment of wastewater and the extended producer responsibility (EPR) scheme for the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries. Parliament stressed the need for a new assessment of the impact of these provisions on the availability of medicinal and cosmetic products, business competitiveness, the stability of supply chains and the costs incurred by consumers and patients. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission intend to perform a new impact assessment verifying the costs of implementing quaternary wastewater treatment or the impact of the EPR scheme on the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries?

What up-to-date data does it have to illustrate the actual contribution of the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries to the release of the micropollutants covered by the directive, and does this data justify saddling these industries with the brunt of the costs?

What steps will it take to ensure that the achievement of environmental objectives does not push up prices, hobble production in the EU or reduce the availability of medicinal and cosmetic products on the EU market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.9.2026) An update study on the cost of quaternary treatment published by the Joint Research Centre in 2025, taking into account updated cost data, the provisions of the final Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (UWWTD)1 compared to the Commission proposal and inflation2 concluded that the impact assessment estimates on extended producer responsibility (EPR) costs remain valid. Work on the assessment of substances in urban wastewater has been part of the preparatory work accompanying the Commission proposal for a revised UWWTD3. The evaluation of the Directive, due by 2033, will consider ‘improved knowledge on the presence of micropollutants in urban wastewater, their impacts (…), as well as data resulting from the new monitoring obligations on micropollutants’4. In line with recital 21 of the recast Directive, Member States should take into consideration the possible impacts of the application of the EPR on the accessibility, availability and affordability of products at national level. The Commission will continue its close cooperation with the European Parliament, Member States and stakeholders on the pragmatic implementation of the recast Directive and will monitor its impact on the accessibility, availability and affordability of products at national level, in particular medicines.
1 Directive (EU) 2024/3019 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2024 concerning

urban wastewater treatment (recast), OJ L, 2024/3019, 12.12.2024. 2 Joint Research Centre (2025) - Updated estimation of the costs of quaternary wastewater treatment in the EU: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC144745. 3 Joint Research Centre (2022): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048969722042218?via%3Dihub; Commission impact assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning urban wastewater treatment (recast) SWD(2022) 541 final. 4 Article 30 of Directive (EU) 2024/3019.
